description: An early Hebridean monastic site, apparently founded by Catan, a follower of Columba, in the 6th or 7th CE. The buildings still standing today are 14th to 15th CE, recent excavations have shown activity from the early 15th CE onwards. No earlier activity has been confirmed archaeologically and the site appears to be at high risk from erosion.
bibliography: Archaeology, Current. “Excavating Eaglais Na H-Aoidhe on the Isle of Lewis | The Past,” June 28, 2025. https://the-past.com/news/excavating-eaglais-na-h-aoidhe-on-the-isle-of-lewis/.
